closest.why: Berglund, Hübsch and Minic, LHEP 2021 (arXiv October 2020), the first refereed statement. The abstract says dark matter 'comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter'. §3 says 'the A fields denote the usual Standard Model fields, and the Ã are their duals', and eq. (8) puts L_m and L̃_dm on one √−g(x). It calls the dual space 'canonically conjugate'. It differs from C1 by building in visible–dual mixing at order λ⁸/L¹⁰, a fermion seesaw, a dual photon 'correlated to the visible photon' and 'correlated events in the accelerators'. It has no gate and no monopoles.

Minic, Belgrade proceedings 2020 (talk September 2019, arXiv February 2020), the earliest written statement. Eqs. (49)–(50) give 'visible and dual (dark) matter in the observed spacetime', and §7 ties 'Standard Model and its dual, describing the dark matter sector' to Born reciprocity in 'spacetime and energy momentum space'. The dark fields couple to the metaparticle's dual momentum p̃. Its dark matter is entangled with visible matter, 'should be detectable', and is identified with modified dark matter.

Hübsch and Minic 2024 (arXiv only). Its polarization language is closest to C1's: 'classical spacetime label x … a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization in modular (quantum) spacetime', with the dual fields as 'fuzzy' dark matter that does not commute with visible fields. It also shows that the dual is not ordinary momentum: 'dual spacetime x̃, [x,x̃]=iλ², and dual momentum space p̃ … (Also, [x,p]=iħ=[x̃,p̃])'.

Berglund, Hübsch and Minic, refereed review (IJMPD 2023). It calls metastring theory an implementation of 'Born reciprocity (the fundamental reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space)'. Each observed particle 'should have a dual particle', and the duals are 'good candidates for dark matter that is correlated to the observed, visible matter'. The record already cites this paper for another purpose.

Freidel, Leigh and Minic, PLB 2014. It says nothing about dark matter, but it is why the school's 'dual' means C1's 'conjugate': the dual coordinates are 'coordinates in momentum space', and T-duality is 'cast essentially as a Fourier transform' (also 1405.3949: the momentum-space picture is 'the choice of a dual Lagrangian submanifold').

conjectures.new_in_conjecture: The published version puts the dark sector on the dual coordinate x̃ of a doubled, string-scale phase space ([x,x̃] = iλ², beside an ordinary momentum p with [x,p] = iħ). It also couples that sector to ours by construction, so it predicts the non-gravitational dark-matter–Standard-Model coupling that would kill C1 (#11 §13 row 7). C1 places dark matter in the momentum polarization of ordinary quantum kinematics (one phase space, conjugate at ħ), coupled to us by gravity alone with a permanent direct-detection null (strict P4), and attributes our x-polarization to spontaneous breaking. C1's two forms carry the physical content that 'organized around momentum' has in it, and no paper found states either: χ particles whose self-interaction is gated in relative velocity (a knee at v*, the island discriminant), and topological monopoles localized in momentum (C2). In the school's effective theory the dual fields are ordinary local fields on spacetime, with no interaction that is local in momentum.
conjectures.published_parts: That dark matter is the Born-reciprocal counterpart of ordinary matter is published by Minic and collaborators. Every Standard Model field has a dual, the duals are the dark matter, and once the dual coordinate is integrated out both sectors sit on one spacetime metric. The claim first appears in Minic's Belgrade proceedings (talk September 2019, arXiv:2003.00318, February 2020), which motivates 'Standard Model and its dual' by Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space. The first refereed statement is Berglund, Hübsch and Minic, LHEP 2021 (arXiv:2010.15610). The school restated it through 2026, once in a Snowmass white paper co-signed by Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman and Leigh (arXiv:2202.06890, February 2022). The founders' own reading of the dual coordinate as momentum space (Freidel, Leigh and Minic 2014) makes their 'dual' C1's 'conjugate'. The older mirror-matter literature has the shape of a copy of ordinary matter coupled mainly through gravity (the panel's Foot 2014 and Berezhiani 2004 reviews), but without reciprocity.

label_disputes.reason: 'each observed quantum field has a “dual”, which could be associated with dark matter degrees of freedom' (quote checked) makes the same claim as 2202.05104 ('dark matter should be viewed as a dual SM') and 2212.06086, which both carry 'anticipates'. Its hedge matches the anchor paper's own ('could be interpreted as dark matter Lagrangian'). It is a restatement citing Minic 2020 and gives no independent priority, but it records that Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman and Leigh co-signed the identification by February 2022.

notes:
Physical-content lens. I read #11 §1, §3–§5, §7.1, §8, §10, §11.4, §12, §13 and App. A items 3–5; the wiki pages for C1, P4, founding supposition 4 and broken Born duality; the notebook's P4 and gate (#1 §1, §3); and popsci #12's 'gravitational influence, and nothing else'. In full text I read the cited school passages (2003.00318 §2.2, §4.1, §4.3, §5, §7; 2010.15610 §1–§5; 2407.06207 §3.3; 2212.06086), FLM 1307.7080 and 1405.3949 for the meaning of x̃, and three related papers (Pavšič 2205.02787, FKLM 2104.00802, and the Sheng Ran entry). Every quote above was checked FOUND with lit.py quote; the list is in panel/c1-content/notes.md.

(1) Is the school's x̃ the momentum side of phase space? Structurally yes, literally no. Freidel, Leigh and Minic read the dual Lagrangian as momentum space and T-duality as a Fourier transform. Berglund, Hübsch and Minic call (x/λ, x̃/λ) 'phase-space' operators with x̃ 'the canonically conjugate dual space'. The program's Born geometry is theirs, and #11 §3 already credits their (x, x̃) polarization as prior art for its own (x, p) polarization, so consistency requires reading their dual sector as the counterpart of conjugate matter. But in the metaparticle behind every dark-matter statement, x̃ is a string-scale coordinate ([x,x̃] = iλ²) next to the ordinary momentum p ([x,p] = iħ = [x̃,p̃]), 'a doubling of the usual phase space coordinates', and the dark fields couple to the dual momentum p̃.

(2) Is 'the dual SM is the dark matter' the same claim as C1? It is the same identification: each visible field has a reciprocity dual, the duals are the dark matter, and at zeroth order in λ both sit on one metric (2010.15610 eq. 8). The physics differs: (a) the dual is a string-scale coordinate, not ordinary momentum; (b) the coupling: the school's sector is correlated with ours by design (mixing terms, seesaw, DM as 'sources' for visible matter, a dual photon correlated with ours, accelerator correlations, MDM's a₀ ~ cH₀, 'should be detectable'), while C1 shares only gravity and predicts a permanent null; (c) the school's dark matter is a full dual SM of fuzzy, non-local metaparticles, ordinary local fields on x after integrating out x̃, while C1's χ clusters in position with a velocity-gated self-interaction, or forms momentum-localized monopoles; (d) the school treats the polarization as a choice, C1 as spontaneous breaking.

Ruling: anticipated. C1 as P.R. states it ('dark matter is conjugate (momentum) matter'; the brief's 'mirror-polarized counterpart … gravitating like ours') is the identification. The school states it in substance, and (a)–(d) are differences of framework and model, which the brief allows when named. Confidence is medium because a reader who counts strict P4 and ordinary momentum at ħ as part of C1's substance would call the published claim a close variant (partly anticipated). Calling the identification new would be the missed-prior-art failure: it is published with equations, in the Born-geometry framework the program itself borrows.

Priority rests on 2003.00318 and 2010.15610; the other 'anticipates' items are restatements with no independent weight. 2610.19522 was posted in October 2026, at the same time as the program's record, so it is not prior art. 2604.19418 (April 2026) is prior. Kept: all 'anticipates' labels; 2111.05659 and 2011.08852 as partial; the two evidence-against items (mild, bearing only on particle χ's 'zero cluster signal', not on the identification); and every related label checked. Pavšič's dark copy comes from an extra quaternionic unit, not the momentum half. Sheng Ran's dark matter is 'not a new particle species'. FKLM 2021 hedges its class II remnants between dark energy and dark matter.
